Aside from focusing on things in your direct experience, you can also suggest yourself into greater alertness (it's still relaxed-alert, not paranoid-alert). Keep your eyes open. Use a small hand movement each time you make the auto-suggestion that you're gaining increasing clarity. Then stop the hand movement and see where your mind is at. That hand movement is the mental escape into the body's flow. Say something like,
“Starting with your eyes open, press your thumb to your forefinger, gently, and let go. Each time you do, you get a little more awake… Press and let go again, a bit clearer. And once more, and now you’re clearer than when you started. Now stop pressing. In the first second after you stop, is the pressing still echoing somewhere? Start with your fingers, which may still be tingling. Did your breath keep the rhythm going? Is your attention still waiting for the next press? Or maybe there’s no echo at all. Just notice. Then sit up straight and work from this level.”

So inner child therapy draws on those higher vantage points more concretely. The inner Guide is the closest thing here to a Higher Self, and it has to work with the Nurturer and Protector and come after them. It can’t act like some transcendent authority that waves everything away. Most reparenting doesn’t do enough with the Guide, and IFS goes to the opposite extreme, so I’m trying to bring together the best of both. IFS isn’t exactly one system, so I may be simplifying it here. It has its own branches and disputes, and that’s one more problem I’m trying to remedy by laying all this out systematically in this guide.
IFS calls these wounded young parts “exiles.” I find that pathologizing. I prefer to speak of a child who needs parenting and integration, rather than naming them by their wounded or excluded condition.
And the parts just keep coming: managers, firefighters, exiles, polarized parts, legacy burdens, Self-energy, guides, new subparts... At some point it’s a maze, with a little one somewhere in the middle of it. Some practitioners are gentle about it and walk you through the maze just fine. Others seem to leave people more split up than when they started. A big institute and a pile of certificates won’t tell you whether a model is true, or whether it’s safe for you.

When the Practice Feels Real but Stays Shallow
Some people have the opposite problem. It feels like you’re connecting with your little one, but the contact is staying near the surface. Meditating for a long time and then sleeping can open up much more emotionally direct stuff, especially in a second sleep, after you’ve already slept once. What showed me that the daytime pl/ork had stayed shallow was the difference at night. Say you wake up from a dream soaked in way more feeling and need than anything the session got near. Then this is probably you. (A nice session that just wears off is a different thing.) I’d ask what the dream let you feel that the session didn’t, and look at it again after your morning coffee. And if nightmares start wrecking your sleep, dial the practice down by doing it earlier in the day, or for less time.

rewrite:
If the Love Isn’t Coming Yet
If you weren’t loved well as a child, “love your inner child” can sound like nonsense. Love them how? Maybe you really want the best for your little one. Maybe you hug them in your imagination, or miss them. And you can still feel none of the warmth people mean when they say love. That doesn’t close the door, though, it just means you start smaller.
Maybe just imagining a caring grown-up makes you feel more threatened, or lonelier. Lonelier is a strange one, with somebody right there. Then go smaller still, to the least cruel response a decent adult could offer your little one. It’s scaffolding, and it isn’t a test of whether you were loved enough.
Once you take the hostility out, there’s room for warmth. What people most often say helped is letting their defenses down. I mean by choice, after the part guarding you has been heard. If you’ve never been safe being loved, your ego can act like a rigid security guard that won’t let the feeling in, and being vulnerable is the opening the feeling needs. (This guard is only about letting the feeling in. People still have to earn your trust.) Sometimes the warmth is there, with a cold part standing in front of it, guarding something. That part tends to step aside once it’s been heard (see the section Hear the Guard First).
If the love still isn’t coming, you can at least stop judging your little one. Obviously no insults. Helpful advice is great, we all need advice. Let them absorb it at their pace. And don’t expect a thank-you for the session, like they booked it. That’s enough to start being the adult, even if it isn’t enough yet for them to trust you. Trust takes warmth, and if there isn’t any yet, borrow some.
Your little one might not take it well at first. 😜 More like “Oh, so NOW you care?” Your first instinct might be “But I’m trying!” Some days, just hearing it out like a decent adult is the only thing you’ll manage to borrow.

rewrite:
Forgiveness without bypass
We cannot force forgiveness on ourselves. It has to come from understanding, otherwise it can be bypassing. But if we stay in the anger forever, we let the injury dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We just remember that it can all be true at once. They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it. Keeping our boundary with them is crucial, especially after forgiveness, since forgiving tends to weaken it. One day we may find that we have forgiven them for not knowing better, just like Jesus did on the Cross.
You might say to the part of you that got hurt, “I’m not going to use spiritual mumbo jumbo to shush your cries and make you forgive before you're ready. But I’m also not going to build our whole life around this wound forever.”
Forgiving yourself
For self-forgiveness, name what you regret doing, and take responsibility for just that part. Let yourself feel the remorse by taking in the harm done, and see how it went against your values. But stop short of making yourself a permanent criminal by identifying with the behaviors you're now abandoning.
Do what you can to put it right. Every so often, come back to how you got to be someone who could do that, until you understand the pattern well enough that it can't drive you anymore.
